method: Opened the registered URLs with browser retrieval; scoped each conclusion to the opened page and its stated date, jurisdiction, product, edition, and evidence type. No claim is marked as blanket accepted.

sourceRegistries.preservedDesign: research/source/Series of Calls communications ecosystem design.md

references.scopedFinding: Feature families and availability vary by plan and cloud; the page lists separate cloud variants and references licensing/availability. Supports family-level profiles, not universal parity.
Documents Calling Plans, Operator Connect, Phone Mobile and Direct Routing as distinct models with different carrier/management responsibilities. Supports modeling these as separate pathways.
Basic and Pro licenses have different capabilities/limits; shared meeting devices require Rooms licenses. Limits are edition-specific and subject to change.

references.pageTitle: Meetings and events in Microsoft Teams
references.scopedFinding: Describes meeting/event types, roles, limits and licensing; page states licensing changes effective 2026-04-01. Avoid carrying old SKU assumptions forward.
Describes cloud contact-center/omnichannel and AI-related features as a Microsoft product reference. Does not validate any simulation capability or competitor equivalence.
Distinguishes Connect, Extend and Unify and lists vendor integrations. Supports distinct integration models, not generic full-contact-center capability for native Teams queues.

Lists Exchange Server, SharePoint Server and Skype for Business Server running on customer-owned Azure Local, with hybrid/disconnected options. Claim that this is not an on-prem Teams edition is not explicit on this page; treat that negative as unresolved absent a direct exclusion statement.

openedSources.accessStatus: opened as a follow-up, non-primary community Q&A
openedSources.use: Supplementary only; answer is anonymous and not an official product specification.

notes: A Microsoft Learn Q&A page with an anonymous answer states that Teams itself has no on-premises version, but this is not a primary product specification and is not treated as sufficient to accept the negative claim.

references.pageTitle: GCC High and DoD service description
references.scopedFinding: Describes defined US government cloud environments, eligibility and feature differences. Supports US-specific profiles; does not support exporting the rules to other jurisdictions.

references.pageTitle: Azure Communication Services retirement and breaking changes
references.scopedFinding: Guide says standalone ACS retirement effective 2028-09-30 and distinguishes retirements/breaking changes from supported Teams-aligned scenarios. Tables are feature-specific; do not generalize that all calling/automation continues.

For Teams meeting Copilot, distinguishes temporary speech processing from saved transcription; E2EE meetings are unsupported. Scope is Teams meeting configuration and applicable licensing/cloud, not all Copilot or vendors.

references.pageTitle: Configure ServiceNow integration for Teams Rooms
references.scopedFinding: Integration is available for Commercial cloud; government cloud guidance points to email/ITSM ingestion instead. Supports an example of integration availability differing from room-device availability.

Lists collaboration workflows (meetings, messaging, calling, webinars, events, etc.) and vendor-described deployment/residency positioning. Marketing page does not substantiate detailed feature/region/security guarantees.

references.pageTitle: Cisco Collaboration Flex Plan 3.0 and Webex Suite data sheet
references.scopedFinding: Lists subscription buying models, bundles/add-ons and cloud/on-prem options; specific tiers differ. Current offers should be modeled as SKU/entitlement-specific.

references.evidenceType: Cisco Help Center product documentation, dated 2026-10-16
references.scopedFinding: Dedicated Instance is a Webex Calling add-on based on UCM architecture and supports older endpoints/integrations; split users across DI and Webex Calling have non-harmonized features. Supports migration/interworking differences, not feature parity.

references.pageTitle: Cisco Collaboration Flex 3.0 Contact Center data sheet
references.scopedFinding: Lists cloud/on-prem contact-center platforms, channels and buying models; named-agent model is Webex Contact Center only and supervisors/admins require Premium Agent. Offer details are version-specific.

Describes CPaaS, channels, flow orchestration, integrations and contact policy. Supports an example of commercial multi-channel engagement and consent/contact thresholds; does not establish channel availability by geography or a universal guarantee.

Claims Cisco devices join Webex, Teams, Zoom and Google Meet through native/certified/CVI experiences. Scope depends on device, mode, licensing and platform; marketing overview alone cannot validate all interoperability functions.

references.evidenceType: Cisco Help Center product/partner guide, dated 2026-08-06
references.scopedFinding: Describes parent/subpartner onboarding, customer provisioning, package offers, partner administration and billing reports. Concrete wholesale example; responsibilities are specific to this programme.

references.pageTitle: Cisco AI PODs for Collaboration datasheet
references.scopedFinding: Describes on-prem transcription and claims air-gap support, but says licensing is an exception to zero external connectivity. Lists language/capacity/integration constraints. Treat as vendor-published, version-specific claims, not independent verification.

references.pageTitle: End-of-Sale and End-of-Life: UCM Cloud for Government
references.scopedFinding: States last order 2027-01-06 and renewal/support through 2028-01-31; offers Webex for Government Calling or on-prem UCM transition options. Time-sensitive product notice, not generalized supplier obsolescence.

references.pageTitle: End-of-Sale and End-of-Life: Cisco Webex WFO
references.scopedFinding: Applies to listed Webex WFO SKUs: last order 2026-07-25, renewal 2027-07-30, support 2031-07-31. Retirement of listed offers does not mean the whole WFO family disappears.

references.pageTitle: Session Border Controllers certified for Direct Routing
references.scopedFinding: Certification/support is limited to listed device and firmware versions; non-certified SBC support may be rejected and vendor is first support path. Certification is distinct from cloud/feature approval.
Reference is a certified-hardware catalogue; certification is device/model-specific and does not by itself establish support for every feature or cloud environment, consistent with the scoped claim.

Documents a separate compliance-recording solution/program; it should be modeled separately from ordinary meeting recording. Details depend on integration/vendor/cloud and are not captured by catalog presence alone.
Marketplace page lists partner solutions by product/category. Presence is ecosystem evidence, not formal certification, security approval, support guarantee or feature parity.

references.evidenceType: Cisco marketplace listing; third-party supplier description
references.assessment: Supported as listing, not independent validation
references.scopedFinding: Listing describes attendant console, recording, fax and analytics integrations, including mixed Cisco environments. It is supplier-supplied listing content; validate account, cloud, feature and commercial prerequisites separately.

references.pageTitle: Theta Lake for Webex Calling listing
references.evidenceType: Cisco marketplace listing; third-party supplier description
references.assessment: Supported as listing, not compliance approval
references.scopedFinding: Listing describes archiving/compliance review for specified Webex Calling, SMS, recordings/CDRs and other products, requiring active Webex Calling plus Theta Lake subscription. It is not a legal-compliance certification.

references.pageTitle: WFM Adapter by TTEC Digital listing
references.evidenceType: Cisco marketplace listing; third-party supplier description
references.scopedFinding: Listing describes RTA and historical-report transfer to third-party WFM (including NICE, Aspect, Verint, Calabrio) and requires a paid Webex Contact Center account/admin. Does not validate forecast quality or all versions.

Current page describes Flow user/device/license provisioning, deprovisioning, role-based delegation, migration and multiple UC connectors. Marketing claims only; exact connector versions and functions need product-specific validation.
Describes automation, migration, provisioning, management, monitoring and analytics across Cisco UC/Webex. Product-page claims, not independent performance/security proof.
Describes policy-driven UC provisioning/lifecycle workflows across Teams, Cisco/Webex, Zoom and other environments. Claims are supplier marketing; do not infer actual certification or effectivity.

Describes self-hosted/air-gapped Cisco Meeting Server management, identity/LDAP, RBAC, multi-tenancy and API automation; states FIPS/DISA/JITC/APL and sub-minute failover. Security/certification/availability claims are vendor assertions, not independently verified here.

references.assessment: Partial; exact feature claims need page-level sources
references.scopedFinding: The exact URL opens a broad documentation index with topics for deployment, offline environments, users/meetings, tenant routing, policies and integrations. It supports existence of documented product/admin areas, but this index alone does not substantiate specific feature behavior or current version.

Describes CVI joining Teams from non-Teams devices and SIP calling from Teams Rooms into cross-platform meetings; mentions sovereign/air-gapped use and multi-tenant deployment. Product claims require scenario/version/tenant validation and are not certification evidence by themselves.

Explicitly differentiates Cloud, Hybrid and self-hosted Government deployment; feature matrix varies by calendar/platform, including GCC/GCC-H/DoD and on-prem Exchange. Strong support for scenario-specific feature matrices, but self-described service claims only.

Page describes a Collaborate portfolio for managing communications/collaboration ecosystems and customer segments. It is a high-level marketing page and provides little feature-level evidence for assurance/monitoring claims.

Catalog lists programmable communications channels, APIs, contact center and engagement products. Catalog supports category overlap only; specific channel, region, price, SLA and product capabilities need their own current documentation.
Catalog lists messaging, voice, email, verification, contact center, APIs and network connectivity. Supports broad category existence only, not detailed availability/pricing or performance claims.

Describes cloud CCaaS with messaging channels, queues/routing, agent roles, history, automations and analytics. Channel list and product functions are product-specific and require current account/region/version validation.
Index links contact-center, WFM, UC, analytics and CPaaS documentation; it is a navigation index rather than substantive evidence. Use linked product docs for any specific mechanic/capability claim.

Describes recording/retention policies, quality/coaching, screen recording, analytics, surveys and workforce scheduling/adherence. Supports WEM capability-family distinction; not proof that all capabilities are present in all licenses/regions.

Describes calendar-connected bot that joins/records/transcribes Zoom, Meet and Teams; bot is visible as a guest, and platform/org guest policies and consent apply. Do not characterize as silent/anonymous or universally permitted.

references.evidenceType: Fireflies Help Center, last updated about six months before check
references.scopedFinding: Lists supported meeting platforms and integration enablement behavior. It is a vendor support list and does not establish consent, privacy, retention, admin approval or availability in regulated clouds.

Describes syncing Teams chats/channels, summaries and reports; work/school account needed for full features and channel access may require admin approval. Adds a third-party identity/data path; not blanket permission.

Distinguishes hosted multitenant service from premium self-hosted service on customer cloud/data center; self-hosted customer owns infrastructure/backups/monitoring and applies updates. Supports distinct operating obligations, not a promise of disconnected use.

references.assessment: Supported with strict scope and approval conditions
references.scopedFinding: Only listed Foundry containers are supported; disconnected use requires access approval, Azure subscription/resource approval and commitment-tier billing; offline usage records must be collected. Scope is these containers, not any Microsoft AI service.

references.assessment: Supported with geography and integration scope
references.scopedFinding: Describes RedSky E911 location/routing for US and Canada and named call platforms; InformaCast pairing adds internal notification. Vendor/partner page, not regulatory suitability or universal emergency-call coverage.

Describes Asterisk as open-source framework for PBX, gateways, conferencing and custom communications; notes developer/system-integrator expertise. Supports framework model, not a ready turnkey/secure solution claim.

Describes a software switching platform; directory, dialplan and module configuration separately govern authentication/routing/behavior. Supports configurable platform model. Product page notes FreeSWITCH Enterprise is commercially supported; does not imply free support.

Current page presents Verint platform and workforce/CX portfolio; the URL/title indicates Verint + Calabrio relationship. It does not show that all products, contracts, support or features became interchangeable. Claim's separation of company ownership and product identity is appropriate.

Describes RingEX as calls/text/video/fax/workplace collaboration with AI and routing. Marketed as an AU page; uptime and integration counts are supplier claims. Does not establish all feature availability, SLA or regulatory fit.

references.assessment: Supported as product profile only; time-sensitive claims
references.scopedFinding: Describes contact-center voice plus 20+ digital channels, AI, WEM, integrations and outbound. Pricing/availability and numeric performance assertions are marketing claims and can change.

Describes enterprise voice, SIP routing, centralized management, on-prem/cloud-connected deployment and current Aura 10.3. Scale/security/compliance statements are supplier assertions; do not infer every deployment has them.

Describes orchestration of customer interactions, data, AI and workflows with deployment/control positioning. Marketing-level reference; architecture, service availability and actual controls need further technical sources.

Describes cloud, on-prem, hybrid and private-cloud business communications, including dedicated secure cloud positioning. Broad portfolio marketing; no evidence of feature parity or compliance approvals.
Lists telephony, conferencing, messaging, mobility and products; page/resources carry different update dates. Supports portfolio presence, not the bundled feature set in every product/market.

Describes self-hosted/hosted phone system, contact center, messaging and integrated AI offerings. Edition/deployment and supported-trunk details vary; marketing page alone cannot verify security or version-specific operation.

references.evidenceType: Meta/WhatsApp Business Platform pricing page; redirected to whatsappbusiness.com
references.scopedFinding: Pricing distinguishes marketing/authentication/utility/service delivered messages and a 24-hour customer-service window; rate varies by market-category. Pricing rules are date/market-sensitive and should be verified from current rate table. Webex Connect's channel support is a separate commercial example.

Lists Workplace, Phone, Rooms, Contact Center, WFM, virtual agent, AI services and AI On-Prem. Supports portfolio breadth only; does not show that Zoom replaces PSTN/provider, specialized requirements, or any one competitor in a given scenario.

references.assessment: Supported with AU scope; page aging noted
references.scopedFinding: Describes risk-based cloud assessment and authorisation, shared responsibility, evidence, assessment and ongoing assurance. Provider evidence informs the accountable authorising officer; it is not blanket acceptance of all customer configurations. Source page published 2020-07-27 and reviewed 2024-01-18.

references.pageTitle: Using a FedRAMP Certified Cloud Service
references.scopedFinding: Reusable FedRAMP evidence does not itself authorize an agency system; agency decides its configuration, integrations and controls and must authorize and monitor its system. US federal context only.

ISMAP evaluates/registers cloud services for government procurement; overview distinguishes main scheme and ISMAP-LIU low-impact SaaS and describes procurement from registered lists in principle. Does not itself prove a specific service is currently listed or suitable.

references.evidenceType: Japanese government ISMAP portal notice, dated 2026-01-09
references.scopedFinding: Says government bodies must address AI-specific risks even for registered services; distinguishes SaaS registration from using an unregistered model on a registered IaaS/PaaS under conditions. Not blanket approval or prohibition.

references.evidenceType: European Data Protection Board SME guidance
references.assessment: Supported with transfer-mechanism scope; no localization claim
references.scopedFinding: Explains transfer criteria and adequacy/safeguards/derogations for transfers outside EEA. It is not a general EU localization rule and does not imply storage location alone determines transfer legality.
